newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-COURSE RECORD FOR JONZON.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-COURSE RECORD FOR JONZON.

text.p: Sweden's Michael Jonzon broke the Druid's Glen course record by a stroke on Friday to elbow his way into a three-way tie for the Irish Open second round lead.

Jonzon, who had hit a barren patch after recording his maiden European Tour success earlier in the year in the Portuguese Open, bogeyed his first hole but then ran in five successive birdies to the turn.
He picked up three more shots coming home for a seven-under-par 64 to move to six-under-par 136. His 64 broke by a stroke the record set in the first round by Britain's Lee Westwood.
Westwood, who was just starting his round as Jonzon signed his card, and Denmark's Thomas Bjorn shared the three-way tie for the lead with the Swede.
"Since winning the Portuguese Open in March I've struggled, especially the big events in Britain when the top European players have been on show," Jonzon said.
"But they are all here this week and I'm glad I'm back where I was in Portugal to show that I can compete with the best."
Bjorn looked as though he would lunch on a two-stroke lead before double- bogeying four holes from home but the Ryder Cup aspirant had to settle for a round of 70 and shared the lead.
Defending champion Colin Montgomerie was two strokes off the pace with a 70 for 138.

Fellow Briton Ian Woosnam, the European rankings leader, lay one-under after a 70 but another former winner Bernhard Langer of Germany, who has won this title three times, slumped out of the event with a 75 for 150.
